director.chapterArc: A high-stakes tactical briefing followed by an ambush where the protagonist executes a forbidden dual-action maneuver to kill a Riftspawn, resulting in immediate physical trauma and magical exhaustion. The scene shifts from urgent instruction to chaotic violence, then to clinical aftermath and arrival at Meridian.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's sensory proximity without adopting his teenage voice; the narrator is older, cooler, and more observant than the protagonist. Differentiate characters by status, rhythm, reserve, and conversational pressure rather than accent or caricature. Avoid 'wonder' tones for magical elements; treat them as physical tools with mechanical costs.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is low and intimate; he speaks to Toren as a mentor sharing a dangerous secret. The tone is protective but firm.
cues.from: Rook told him the other thing at first light, sitting on the ground with his back against the sixth block, in about two minutes, and did not look at him once while he said it.
cues.through: "You asked me at a fire," he said. "Thirteen days old, with a bowl in your hands. You said you did both, and I said everybody's mostly right about most things, and I told you to eat your food. I've thought about that four hundred times since and I've never once been sorry, because you'd have spent the whole summer trying to do it, and you'd have put it out, and you'd have decided it wasn't for you, and it is for you, and I'd have taken it off you with one sentence on a riverbank in the dark."

cues.delivery: Rook delivers a technical lesson with flat affect. The rhythm is staccato and precise as he lists the four sentences of instruction.
cues.from: "Dessa asked me on a bridge what it was called and I said it isn't called anything and then I was rude to her, and the first part was true and the second part was mine. It isn't called anything. There's nothing to name. It is not a third thing you do instead of the two. It's what's there when you stop doing the two.
cues.through: "Three. So don't ask. Have somewhere to be, and go there, and don't stop halfway to find out which half of you is doing the carrying."

cues.delivery: Rook's tone hardens as he delivers the final warning. The pause before 'Don't do it' carries significant weight.
cues.from: "Four," he said. "It'll cost. I don't know how much. I watched a girl do it for the first time in a valley with instruments on her, and she was fifteen, and she'd had four years of the best instruction there has ever been in this world, and it put her on a floor for two days, and when she got up she said it had been worth it, and she was lying, and I knew she was lying and I didn't say so because she'd have hit me."
cues.through: "And the last thing, and it's the only one I'd go back and die for getting wrong." He turned his head then, finally, and looked at him. "Don't do it.

cues.delivery: Rook's voice is authoritative and clipped. He assigns roles with absolute certainty; no rising inflection for questions.
cues.from: "Wyck at the mule's head, because Dessa can't run and he can, and because if Pitch goes we need somebody at that head who won't let go. Dessa at the tailgate with her hands on the boards and her eyes shut, and she calls, and nobody argues with a call, and nobody asks her to explain one. Toren out on the east flank at forty yards, because forty yards is far enough that it has to choose.
cues.through: "Here's the condition and then I'll shut up. If it gets to the cart, that's the end of it. Not the end of the cart. The end. There is nobody on this pasture who can stop that thing twice, and I am the only one who can stop it once, and once is what there is."

cues.delivery: Senna's voice is frail but sharp. She speaks with dry irony and clinical precision about the odds.
cues.from: Senna said, from under the blankets, "And if it comes at the cart, I should like everybody to keep walking."
cues.through: "No," said Senna Voss. "I didn't think you would. But it'll be said now, won't it, and nobody can pretend afterward that it wasn't."

cues.delivery: Dessa's voice is flat and matter-of-fact. The shift from 'Thirty feet' to the threat must be seamless but chilling.
cues.from: Then Dessa said, "Thirty feet," in an absolutely ordinary voice, and then, without any change at all in the voice, "it's under the road."
cues.through: It came out of the grip forty feet in front of the mule.

cues.delivery: Action accelerates. The narration becomes fragmented and staccato to match the speed of the attack.
cues.from: Wyck had the head. Wyck was one-armed and the arm was the broken one, and he was fifteen, and he got both his boots into the road and hauled the mule's head round toward the rail with the whole of his weight on the cheek strap, and Wyck Tanner did not run, and it made absolutely no difference at all.
cues.through: It was over in a second and a half. The mule went down in the traces and took the near shaft with him and the cart went over onto the rail with its off wheel in the air, and the tailgate came off its pins, and Dessa went down under the boards, and Senna Voss and four months of blankets and the whole contents of a family's road came out of the bed and across the wet surface of a six-lane in the open with no wall anywhere on any of it.

cues.delivery: Rook's action is described with clinical detachment. The barrier creation feels physical and immediate.
cues.from: And Rook — who had come out of that bed with the rest of it and was lying half across the old woman with his face in the road — got his left hand down flat on the surface of the six-lane and shut it.
cues.through: The thing hit it and stopped.

cues.delivery: Internal realization. The pacing slows slightly to let the trap's logic land before Toren acts.
cues.from: And he understood the trap in the whole of his body before any of it reached his head, which was this: that the wall was the only thing on that pasture keeping any of them alive, and that the wall was a bonfire on a hill, and that it would go on being a bonfire on a hill until Rook was finished, and that Rook would be finished in about four minutes, and that the thing had no reason in the world ever to go anywhere else.
cues.through: "Four minutes," Rook said, into the road, not loudly, to nobody.

cues.delivery: Toren's action is frantic but grounded. The shouting is urgent, not panicked.
cues.through: "Get her up," he shouted back, over his shoulder, already forty yards out and going. "Get her up and get her to the berm — Elias! — let it go, let it go, I've got it—"

cues.delivery: Rapid succession of tactical errors. The narration mirrors Toren's confusion and physical failure.
cues.from: He was out past the wire by then with the fence line on his left and open grass everywhere else, and it came at him across a hundred yards in something under two seconds, and forty feet out its blade-limb went slack and dropped and trailed, and Toren thought the legs, it's the legs, it's already going and put himself two paces to the right of where he was standing, and it went past him at full speed and took the fence and forty feet of wire with it.
cues.through: But the grass was wet and it was not eleven feet of cropped turf between two concrete blocks, and his heel went, and he was an inch and a half slower than he had been the day before, and the edge went through the back of his right thigh on its way past.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue slows to a halt. The realization of the 'wind-up' is delivered with absolute clarity.
cues.through: And the question came up out of him the way it had come up ten thousand times on a verge in the wrong light with a man counting halves at him from a cart bed — which one, put one down, pick the other up, which one, which —

cues.delivery: The dual-action sequence. The rhythm is fluid and continuous; no pauses for breath as Toren executes the impossible.
cues.through: There was nothing to read, and it had never in its existence met a thing with nothing to read, and it came on anyway because coming on was all it had, and Toren went past the edge on the inside with the struts firing off the crash rail and the wet iron, and he was behind its shoulder with the root of that limb extended and open and four inches from his hand.

cues.delivery: Violence described clinically. The destruction of the Riftspawn is physical and messy.
cues.from: It hit him and he went up and over the crash rail and into the grip, and his left forearm broke on the rail on the way, and he came down in three feet of dead grass and rusty water with everything in him disconnected and the spike gone out of his hand somewhere and his ears full of a sound like a flyover being hit.
cues.through: The whole of it came apart at once. It did not fall. It stopped being a thing that was holding itself in a shape, all at the same instant, the way a knot comes out when you pull the right end, and four hundred pounds of Riftspawn went to a fine drifting grey that did not blow away, and it came down into the grip and over Toren and into the rusty water and filled the ditch from one side to the other, and pooled, and ran along the camber of the road bed above him, and found the low places, and lay there with a shine on it.

cues.delivery: Dessa's voice is quiet and exhausted. The dialogue is sparse; the emotional weight is in what isn't said.
cues.from: Dessa got to him first, on a bad leg, over three hundred yards of wet pasture, and she was the one who went down into the grip with him and got his head up out of the ash, and she did not say anything for a while and neither did he.

cues.delivery: The description of the stone's coldness is tactile and heavy. The narrator emphasizes the physical sensation.
cues.from: It was in the ash beside his hip. Dessa found it and put it in his hand and he closed his fingers round it, and it was cold.
cues.through: Not cool. Not the low unbothered coolness it had carried through four months of road, the way the inside of a well is cool. It was cold the way a stone is cold, the way any stone in that ditch was cold, the way it had been in a fire at seven in the morning on the second of the month before it ever opened, and there was nothing in it, and when he asked it for the shape it had given him ten thousand times without being asked twice, it did not answer, and he could not feel the place where the asking went.

cues.delivery: Rook's reassurance is firm but weary. He speaks with the weight of experience.
cues.through: "No," said Rook. "It isn't. It's what I've got, and I'm not going to improve it by being confident at you."

cues.delivery: The group's movement is slow and laborious. The narration reflects the physical exhaustion.
cues.from: They left the rest of it in a road. There was nothing on that pasture to carry it in, and there was a boy who could not walk and an old woman on a tailgate and a man who could not lift either of them, and Dessa stood at the edge of the grip for a moment looking at three or four hundred pounds of lifted ash going slowly silver in the low places and did the arithmetic out loud, because she was Dessa Cole.
cues.through: Wyck and Dessa had the tailgate with Senna on it, one-armed and bad-legged between them, and it took them eleven rests. Toren came behind on Rook's shoulder, which was the wrong shoulder, and the two of them moved at about the speed of one very old man and fell over twice.

cues.delivery: Rook's final instruction is barely audible. The tone is urgent but controlled; a command to survive.
cues.from: "Don't say anything," said Rook, very quietly, without moving his mouth. "Not one of you. Not a word about the field, not a word about me, not a word about what he's just done out there, until somebody asks a question with a name attached to it."
cues.through: "Because I have stood in front of this gate once before," said Rook, "and they wrote my name in a book, and I have spent eleven years being extremely glad that nobody at that wall ever once asked me what I could do."

pauses.after: The grey was in his mouth and in his eyes and in his ears and it made his back teeth hum, and he understood, distantly and with no interest at all, that he was lying in more money than his family had ever had.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after the creature's destruction.

pauses.after: "I had my eyes shut," she said. "I had my eyes shut the whole way because he told me to, and I felt you at the edge of thirty feet doing it, and it went — I don't know what it did, I'll never be able to say what it did." She wiped his face with her sleeve, which made it worse. "Don't do it again."
pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause for Dessa's warning to land.
Emphasis on the warning; isolation of the command.

pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Rook's physical contact and silence.
